# Influint channel intelligence

An evidence base about what actually moves YouTube performance, built from measured
retention curves rather than from advice. 246 channels are tracked and
19 carry per-video retention analysis. Every claim carries how well it has
held up, on how many independent channels, and what it does not establish.

READ THIS FIRST. Most of this knowledge base has never been quantified. That is the
honest state of it, not a gap being papered over. A claim the battery cannot measure
sits on the record because a practitioner asserted it, and is labelled as such.

The probe battery reaches retention curves, runtime, publish dates and upload cadence,
view counts, titles, the first minute of speech, format libraries, click-through rate,
average view duration and average percentage viewed, the position of a detected
sponsor read or payoff and the last 8% of the curve as an outro. Outside it: the
thumbnail as an image, anything else on screen, revenue and a viewer's internal
motive. Neither reachable nor out of reach, and published as exactly that — in the
store, read by no probe: impressions, net subscriber change, engaged views and watch
time. impressions: 3,702 videos across 19 channels carry a first-28-day impression
count beside their CTR (measured 2026-09-11). Read by the autoresearch vocabulary, not
the battery: frontier.ts registers an `impressions` accessor and the harness has
scored with it. net subscriber change: 3,937 videos carry a first-28-day net
subscriber change and 3,939 carry a lifetime one, across the 19 Studio-pulled channels
(measured 2026-09-11). Read by the autoresearch vocabulary, not the battery:
frontier.ts registers `subs-per-view` over the same field, with views declared as its
denominator so the same-series gate refuses the rate against its own divisor. engaged
views: 3,937 videos carry a first-28-day engaged-view count beside their view count,
on the same 19 channels (measured 2026-09-11). Read by the autoresearch vocabulary,
not the battery: frontier.ts registers `engaged-share`, and it is a near-constant
column — the frontier's tie-mass ceiling discards it on all but two channels, so the
quantity is present and nearly always carries no variation to measure. watch time:
3,937 videos carry first-28-day watch-time hours and 3,939 carry the lifetime figure,
on the same 19 channels (measured 2026-09-11). Read by the autoresearch vocabulary,
not the battery: frontier.ts registers `watch-time-hours`. It is the one of the four
closest to a duplicate of something measured — watch time is views times average view
duration, and the battery reads AVD directly — so an accessor here needs a reason it
is not the identity.

Never present a claim as established without checking its standing and its limits.

## Connect over MCP (recommended)

One file, no dependencies, Node 18 or newer.

1. Download: https://majieddd.github.io/influint-channels-public/yt-intelligence-mcp.mjs
2. Ask your contact at Influint for an API key. It is read-only.
3. Add to your MCP client config:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "yt-intelligence": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/yt-intelligence-mcp.mjs"],
      "env": {
        "YT_INTELLIGENCE_URL": "<ask Influint for the API host>",
        "YT_INTELLIGENCE_KEY": "<your key>"
      }
    }
  }
}

For Claude Code: claude mcp add yt-intelligence --env YT_INTELLIGENCE_URL=<ask Influint for the API host> --env YT_INTELLIGENCE_KEY=<your key> -- node /absolute/path/to/yt-intelligence-mcp.mjs

## Connect over HTTP

NOTE: this build has no API host configured, so the address below is a
placeholder. Ask your contact at Influint for the host as well as the key.

Every endpoint is GET, returns JSON, and needs a bearer token:

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <your key>" "<ask Influint for the API host>/state"

- GET /api/intelligence/state
  tool name: intelligence_state (over HTTP the path segment is `state`; both spellings resolve)
  category: orient
  params: none
  How much of the knowledge base is measured, how many claims share one test, and
  what is waiting on a human. Call it first.
  returns: One object of counts, plus the sentence saying what is measurable at all.

- GET /api/intelligence/catalogue
  tool name: intelligence_catalogue (over HTTP the path segment is `catalogue`; both spellings resolve)
  category: channels
  params: none
  What is here, how good it is, and how it may be used: state, every channel and the
  workflow register, in one call.
  returns: The state answer, the channel list and the workflow register, verbatim.

- GET /api/intelligence/vocabulary
  tool name: intelligence_vocabulary (over HTTP the path segment is `vocabulary`; both spellings resolve)
  category: orient
  params: none
  Every legal value: standings, categories, niches, probe ids, unit nouns, and each
  tool's caps with the reason.
  returns: The legal values of every parameter, the ladder's thresholds, the caps,
  and the refusal rules.

- GET /api/intelligence/claims
  tool name: intelligence_claims (over HTTP the path segment is `claims`; both spellings resolve)
  category: claims
  params: niche, category, standing, measuredOnly, limit, prohibitionLimit
    niche (string) — The channel's marketplace, e.g. maker-build, vlog-lifestyle,
      true-crime. Dialects are canonicalised (woodworking becomes maker-build).
      Open: the legal set is the niches the store actually carries, which this table
      cannot enumerate without reading it — the vocabulary tool does. An unknown
      niche is NOT refused, because most confirmed marketplaces carry no niched
      claim and refusing would reject valid ones; it matches nothing niched and the
      `routing` line on the answer says so in those words.
    category (string) — One claim category, e.g. retention, packaging, ideation,
      production. Open: the legal set is the categories present in the store, which
      the vocabulary tool lists with a count each. An unknown one is not refused —
      the `routing` line says no claim carries it, which is worth reading, because
      an unmatched category empties the prohibitions too.
    standing (string) — Return only claims at one rung of the evidence ladder. One
      of: law, candidate-law, warning, theory.
    measuredOnly (boolean) — Only claims with a reading behind them. Accepts
      true/1/yes or false/0/no; anything else is refused. Default false.
    limit (number) — How many claims come back. Default 60.
    prohibitionLimit (number) — How many refuted claims come back. Separate from
      `limit`, which never reached them: on the live store 14 of 39 were unreachable
      at any `limit` until this parameter existed. Default 25.
  The claims that apply to a channel, routed by niche, WITH the prohibitions: things
  our own data refuted. Says what it omitted.
  returns: The matching claims, the prohibitions that travel with every answer, and
  a line naming anything a cap dropped.

- GET /api/intelligence/claim?id=<id>
  tool name: intelligence_claim_evidence (over HTTP the path segment is `claim`; both spellings resolve)
  category: claims
  params: id (required)
    id (string) — The claim id, from the claims tool. Required.
  One claim's full record: the probe, every per-unit reading, the niche breakdown,
  and an explicit list of what it does NOT establish.
  returns: The claim, its probe, every counted reading, the niche split, and its
  limits.

- GET /api/intelligence/channels
  tool name: list_channels (over HTTP the path segment is `channels`; both spellings resolve)
  category: channels
  params: none
  Every channel in the knowledge base, with niche, scale band and analysis depth.
  returns: One row per channel, largest catalogue first.

- GET /api/intelligence/actions?channelId=<UC...>
  tool name: channel_action_list (over HTTP the path segment is `actions`; both spellings resolve)
  category: channels
  params: channelId (required)
    channelId (string) — A YouTube channel id. Required.
  The prioritised moves for one channel, ordered by viewers recoverable, each with
  the confidence behind it.
  returns: The channel, what the advice rests on, the ordered actions, and the
  dimensions that came back clean.

- GET /api/intelligence/channelBrief?channelId=<UC...>
  tool name: channel_brief (over HTTP the path segment is `channelBrief`; both spellings resolve)
  category: channels
  params: channelId (required)
    channelId (string) — A YouTube channel id. Required.
  The action list with every cited claim's evidence and limits already attached. One
  call instead of one per claim.
  returns: The action list, each action carrying the claim it cites, plus a note on
  what the attached evidence covers.

- GET /api/intelligence/workflows
  tool name: list_workflows (over HTTP the path segment is `workflows`; both spellings resolve)
  category: workflows
  params: none
  The ways this system is operated, each with what it looks at and the ONLY modes it
  may apply a claim in. Read this first.
  returns: The register, one row per workflow.

- GET /api/intelligence/workflow?id=<id>
  tool name: workflow_intelligence (over HTTP the path segment is `workflow`; both spellings resolve)
  category: workflows
  params: id (required), niche, limit
    id (string) — A workflow id from the workflows tool, e.g. video-suggestion.
      Required.
    niche (string) — The channel's marketplace, so the claims are routed the way
      the workflow would route them. Open: the legal set is the niches the store
      carries, which the vocabulary tool lists. An unknown one is not refused; it
      simply matches no niched claim. To route by a CHANNEL's own confirmed
      marketplace rather than one you chose, use the workflow-context tool instead
      of this parameter.
    limit (number) — How many claims come back in each bucket. Default 40.
  The claims one workflow may apply, bucketed by mode: rules, priors (with
  evidence), hypotheses, prohibitions, do-not-repeat.
  returns: Five buckets by application mode, what was left out, and what standing
  withheld.

- GET /api/intelligence/workflowContext?channelId=<UC...>&workflowId=<id>
  tool name: workflow_context (over HTTP the path segment is `workflowContext`; both spellings resolve)
  category: channels
  params: channelId (required), workflowId (required), limit
    channelId (string) — A YouTube channel id. Required.
    workflowId (string) — A workflow id from the workflows tool, e.g.
      video-suggestion. Required.
    limit (number) — How many claims come back in each bucket. Default 40.
  One workflow, routed by a channel's OWN confirmed niche, with the registry row and
  the mode contract. Three calls in one.
  returns: The channel row, how it was routed, the registry entry, the bucketed
  claims, and the mode contract.

A 503 means the API is switched off on that deployment, not that your key is wrong.
A 401 means the key is missing or wrong. Both responses say which.

A 400 means a parameter was refused, and it names the value, the legal values and
the tool's own parameter list. Nothing here answers 200 with an empty list because
a value was mistyped: a guess that looks like an answer is the expensive failure.

A 404 on a tool hands back this whole catalogue, so a wrong name costs one call.

Tools are grouped in categories and this API serves only the read ones: `orient`,
`channels`, `claims`, `workflows`. The `derive` and `remeasure` categories are never
mounted over HTTP at all, whichever file a tool in them is added to:

  derive — Writes a derived artefact (one local-model call, idempotent,
    reversible) beside the evidence rather than into it.
  remeasure — Re-derives standings from stored curves. Pure arithmetic, no API and
    no model calls — and it MOVES standings.

## How to read an answer

- standing: Where a claim sits on the evidence ladder. theory = nobody has measured it. candidate-law = measured once with a real effect. law = reproduced across channels AND signed by a person. warning = a known failure mode. Standing moves DOWN as well as up.
- evidence.units / unitNoun: How many INDEPENDENT things the reading rests on, and what kind of thing. Three readings from one crawl are not three channels, so the noun is never assumed.
- evidence.causalRung: What kind of claim the evidence can support: correlation, consistent, dose-response, temporal, intervention. Earned by the DESIGN of the test, never read off the effect size. A hundred consistent correlations are still a correlation.
- evidence.grade: How much the evidence supports ACTING: untested, weak, moderate, strong. Separate axis from causalRung, deliberately.
- limits: What this claim does NOT establish, generated from its own record. Read it before repeating the claim as fact.
- prohibitions: Claims our data refuted. These travel with every answer because they are the most valuable thing here and the easiest to leave behind.

## What it will not do

It is read-only, and that is the safety boundary rather than a limitation. It cannot
start an analysis, publish anything, or move a claim's standing. Standing moves on a
measurement or on a human signature; an endpoint that let a caller edit it would make
both meaningless.
